title: What Are High-Touch Surfaces?
excerpt: High-touch surfaces are surfaces that people contact frequently with their hands. The exact list depends on how a particular facility is used.
content_html:
High-touch surfaces are surfaces that have frequent contact with hands. The category is based on actual use, not on the size or visibility of the surface. A small door handle may be higher priority than a large wall because many people touch the handle repeatedly.

Common examples

  • Door and cabinet handles.
  • Light switches and control buttons.
  • Handrails and grab rails.
  • Shared touchscreens, keypads and controls.
  • Desk or counter contact points used repeatedly.
  • Washroom handles, taps and other frequently handled fixtures.

The exact list changes by environment. A warehouse, office, school, hotel and healthcare facility will not have identical touch patterns.

High-touch versus low-touch

Low-touch surfaces have relatively little hand contact. Examples can include upper wall areas, ceilings and some window surfaces. CDC healthcare guidance distinguishes high-touch and low-touch surfaces because exposure potential affects cleaning frequency and rigor.

Touch frequency is not the only factor

A high-touch label helps prioritise attention, but the cleaning plan should also consider contamination probability, how many people share the surface, the vulnerability of users, the material and whether the surface is visibly soiled.

High-touch lists should be local

A generic list is a starting point, not a finished schedule. Staff should observe how the building is actually used. A printer release button, lift control or shared latch may become an important touchpoint even if it never appears on a standard checklist.

Practical takeaway

Treat 'high-touch' as an exposure category. Identify what people repeatedly touch in your own facility, then use that information to set suitable cleaning frequency and verification.

References

  1. CDC — When and How to Clean and Disinfect a Facility
  2. CDC — Environmental Services
